WATERS

Every kind of water, explained.

Rivers, lakes, flats, surf, ice and open ocean. See how each one fishes, what to bring and where to go next.

285 TRIP GUIDES

Rivers & streams

Find fish behind rocks, along current seams, and under banks. Learn simple drifts, useful lures, and safe ways to work a river.

Understand this water ↗18 TRIP GUIDES

Spring-fed streams

Get close without spooking fish. Read weed channels, match the hatch, and make clean drifts through clear spring-fed water.

Understand this water ↗2 TRIP GUIDES

Glacier-influenced rivers

Work tributary mouths, softer seams, and clear side water. Adjust your tackle to visibility and leave room for changing flows.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Backcountry & small streams

Find trout in pocket water, shaded bends, and plunge pools. Carry a light kit, make short casts, and leave time for the walk back.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Tailwaters (below dams)

Fish the seams below dams with controlled drifts and simple rigs. Check releases, watch the level, and keep a clear route out.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Big rivers

Break a broad river into seams, backwaters, and deep edges. Choose solid bank access and simple rigs for fish beside the heavy current.

Understand this water ↗25 TRIP GUIDES

Tropical floodplains

Work lagoon mouths, flooded timber, and draining creeks. Match lures to the local predator and let water levels guide the day.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Ponds & small lakes

Find bass, bluegill, and stocked trout close to home. Fish shade and weed edges with a small kit and a few easy presentations.

Understand this water ↗243 TRIP GUIDES

Lakes & reservoirs

Find fish on points, weed edges, and drop-offs. Use simple depth control to make better casts from a bank or boat throughout the day.

Understand this water ↗12 TRIP GUIDES

Alpine lakes

Choose a fish-filled lake, pack a small tackle box, and work the shore for cruising trout while you keep weather and the hike in view.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Great Lakes

Choose a shore, harbor, or boat approach for trout, salmon, perch, and walleye. Follow local seasons, bait, and changing water conditions.

Understand this water ↗12 TRIP GUIDES

Ice fishing

Choose a checked route, drill with a plan, and work small jigs at the right depth. Stay warm and keep rescue gear close at hand.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Canals & urban water

Work bridge shade, canal junctions, and park banks with a compact kit. Find legal access, choose the local target, and keep casts tidy.

Understand this water ↗71 TRIP GUIDES

Estuaries & mangroves

Find fish along mangrove shade, creek mouths, and channel edges. Match your casts to the tide and keep roots and seagrass intact.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Bayous & coastal marsh

Find redfish and other marsh fish around drains, grass points, and deeper bends. Work shallow rigs and plan your return with the tide.

Understand this water ↗35 TRIP GUIDES

Saltwater flats

Learn to spot tails, shadows, and moving fish on shallow flats. Lead the fish with a light lure or fly and stay ready for the first run.

Understand this water ↗14 TRIP GUIDES

Surf & beaches

Find troughs, cuts, and feeding lanes close to shore. Choose a simple bait rig or lure and fish the beach without chasing distance.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Piers, jetties & bridges

Fish pilings, shade lines, and current breaks with simple rigs. Plan the landing first and leave room for waves, boats, and other anglers.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Rocky shores & kelp

Find nearshore fish around rock, kelp, and open pockets. Control lure depth, protect your leader, and choose a shore with room to retreat.

Understand this water ↗70 TRIP GUIDES

Reef & bottom

Work reef edges, wrecks, and deep bottom with controlled drops. Choose the right weight, feel the bite, and prepare fish for release.

Understand this water ↗84 TRIP GUIDES

Offshore

Look for bait, birds, current edges, and floating cover. Learn the basics of trolling, casting, and working with an offshore crew.

Understand this water ↗WATER GUIDE

Kayak fishing

Use a kayak to reach lake edges, sheltered bays, and gentle rivers. Set up a clean deck, control your drift, and land fish from a seat.
